newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria may peg lev to dlr, mark or Swiss franc.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria may peg lev to dlr, mark or Swiss franc.

text.p: Bulgaria's government on Saturday debated pegging its currency, the lev, to the dollar, the German mark or the Swiss frank as part of preparations to introduce a fixed exchange rate regime, a government statement said.

Under a $548 million 20-month standby agreement sealed with the IMF last month, Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a self-regulating restrictive monetary mechanism, known as a currency board, aimed to restore confidence in the financial system.

"The Financial Stabilisation Council considered possible options for pegging the lev to a specific currency after the introduction of a currency board, namely the U.S. dollar, the German mark or the Swiss franc," said the statement.
The council, set up by the caretaker cabinet two months ago, is headed by interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski and includes senior bankers and the finance minister.

Under the currency board system the lev will be pegged to an anchor currency, at a rate that cannot be adjusted. The amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.

An International Monetary Fund (IMF) technical mission to advise the central bank is expected in Sofia next week, said the IMF. An IMF policy mission is expected by mid-May to finalise preparations for introduction of the currency board.
The reformist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), which won an outright parliamentary majority in April 19 elections, is expected to form a cabinet by May 20 to be headed by it leader Ivan Kostov.

The cabinet is expected to set the exchange rate and the anchor currency jointly with the IMF and pass it to parliament for approval along with the other legal amendments needed to make the board operational.

Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance has improved in the past month and the 1997 budget frame agreed with the interim cabinet in March will need to be adjusted to the new indicators, government officials said.

First signs of stability were seen after the two-month rule of the caretaker cabinet, which brought down monthly inflation to 12 percent in March from 243 percent in February and stopped the fall of the lev from an all-time low of 3,000 per dollar in February to around 1,500 now. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
